subject: Mathematics
title: More and Less
subtitle: Longer, higher, heavier, holds more
hero_picture: A Kerala family under a big jackfruit tree heavy with jackfruits: a father holding a long stick, children with a short stick, a mother picking up a jackfruit.

sections.heading: Longer and shorter
text: Dad wants to pluck a big jackfruit.
His stick is longer. My stick is shorter.
A longer stick reaches higher fruits.
sections.caption: A long stick and a short stick
sections.picture: A father and a boy each holding a stick near a jackfruit tree: the father's stick is clearly much longer than the boy's stick.

sections.heading: Higher and lower
text: A longer string lets a kite fly higher.
sections.caption: Kites high in the sky
sections.picture: Five children on a green hill flying kites; one kite flying much higher than all the others.

sections.heading: Heavy and light
text: I cannot lift this big jackfruit. It is heavy.
Amma lifts it. I carry a mango.
sections.caption: Heavy jackfruit, light mango
sections.picture: A girl unable to lift a big heavy jackfruit while her mother lifts it; the girl carries a small light mango instead.

sections.heading: Up and down
text: A monkey and an elephant sit on a seesaw.
sections.caption: Seesaw in the park
sections.picture: A seesaw in a park with a small monkey on one end up in the air and a baby elephant on the other end down on the ground.

sections.heading: Which holds more?
text: Dad made lime juice in a big glass and a small glass.
The big glass holds more juice.
A bucket holds more water than a cup.
sections.caption: Big glass and small glass
sections.picture: A father pouring lime juice into a big glass and a small glass on a table; the big glass holds clearly more juice.

rhyme: For higher fruits, a longer stick,
For higher kites, a string that's thick,
For heavy things, strong arms to lift,
For lots to drink, a big pot, quick!
activity: Find two pencils at home. Put them side by side. Which one is longer?
talk: Which is heavier, a jackfruit or a mango?
Which holds more water, a bucket or a cup?
summary: We can compare things: longer or shorter, heavier or lighter, more or less.

questions.explanation: A jackfruit is much heavier than a mango.

questions.prompt: To pick a fruit high up, we need a...
On a seesaw, which side goes down?

questions.explanation: A bucket holds much more water.

questions.prompt: A big glass and a small glass are full. Which has more juice?
questions.explanation: The big glass holds more juice.
